title: Felix and the Garden
premise: Marguerite Pemberton has spent her life in Thornvale, a valley warded against magic, hiding her gift for speaking with beasts. When her date's name appears in a century-old book of prophecies, she is pulled through the veil into the realm of Aldenmere, where the covenant binding humans, beasts, and fae has shattered — and she is its prophesied mender. Hunted by the Crown's truth-wardens and betrayed by the beast who raised her, Marguerite discovers the covenant was broken deliberately by those who feared what unity would cost them. In the end she must choose between restoring the old law or forging a new covenant sealed with her own memory of home, sacrificing the valley that kept her safe to give both realms a future.
about_author: B. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval bestiaries before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse in the Cotswolds, where they claim the local foxes answer back.

chapters.title: The Date Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the eve of her first date in years, her grandmother's forbidden grimoire opens itself to a prophecy naming tonight — and the man across the café table. A beast-speaker's whisper summons a stag through the valley wards, and Marguerite is dragged through the veil as Thornvale seals behind her. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into terror as the safe world closes forever.

chapters.title: What the Beasts Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Bramble, the fox-spirit who raised her and now serves the Crown. Marguerite learns the covenant between realms broke a century ago when the fae queen was silenced; the beasts remember the truth, but speaking it is treason. She finds allies among outcast creatures in the Sunken Court. Emotional beat: loyalty tested as Bramble denies knowing her, and she realizes even memory can be weaponized.

chapters.title: The Trial Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Captured by truth-wardens, she is judged not by the Crown's courts but by an old rite where beasts themselves testify — their memories made visible to all. The trial exposes the queen's silencing and Bramble's coerced betrayal, igniting rebellion. To reforge the covenant, a speaker must pay in memory, and Marguerite volunteers what she treasures most: Thornvale itself. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: A Covenant of Small Voices
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, closing with Bramble's. At the Worldroot, she speaks the new covenant — not decreed by queens or crowns, but sworn by every creature willing to listen. Her memories of the valley dissolve as magic returns to both realms, yet Bramble, freed from his oath, carries one stolen memory back to her: the sound of her grandmother's voice. Emotional beat: bittersweet homecoming — she cannot return to Thornvale, but Thornvale, changed, comes to her.
